title: A constant adic quotient realization reflects isomorphisms of maps
statement: Under the hypotheses of the constant quotient realization statement, a morphism of the two derived coefficient objects is an isomorphism whenever its constant adic quotient realization is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 093J and 03Q3, the nonempty-chart stalk detection part

proof.text: On W.left, let U be the identity pro-etale object. Its empty sieve is not covering: every generating pro-etale covering family is jointly surjective, so the supplied point has a preimage in a member. If two constants have equal sheafified sections at U, the sheafification unit makes their equalizer sieve covering. If the constants differ this sieve is empty, a contradiction. Naturality of the unit then proves that the ordinary constant functor to sheaves of B-modules on W.left is faithful, for B = A/I^(n+1). This is the private proved helper constantSheaf_faithful_of_point; it does not require connectedness or nonzero B.

Write C for constantAdicQuotientModules X d n, P for the ordinary identified-coefficient module pullback along h = W.hom followed by g, and Q for restriction of scalars along constantAdicQuotientMap. Restriction along the pulled-back finite coefficient comparison commutes with P by proEtaleRingRestrictionPullbackInv_isIso. The proved relativeEncoding helper of the finite-pullback-constructibility module identifies pullback followed by constant-scalar restriction with fixed-module sheaf inverse image. The proved constantEncodingNatIso helper of the adic-lisse-relative-restriction module identifies constant module sheafification followed by that restriction with the ordinary constant-sheaf functor. Cancel the coefficient comparison and its inverse using proEtaleScalarEquivalence.counitIso. Finally uniqueness of left adjoints, using globalSectionsLowerStarIso, identifies inverse image of a constant sheaf with the constant sheaf on W.left. Whiskering these four natural isomorphisms gives (C followed by P followed by the two coefficient encodings) naturally isomorphic to Q followed by the constant-sheaf functor on W.left. These helpers are already proved in their imported modules; their constructibility and adic-lissity main theorems are not invoked.

Restriction of scalars Q is faithful for every ring map, so step 1 makes the right side of the comparison in step 2 faithful. Transport faithfulness across that natural isomorphism and cancel the postcomposed encoding functor to show C followed by P is faithful. A faithful functor reflects monomorphisms and epimorphisms; since the coefficient module category is abelian and balanced, this ordinary realization reflects isomorphisms. Neither bijectivity of the completion-quotient map nor a lifting of arbitrary realized morphisms is needed.

Both C and P are exact. Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso identifies the given realization with the derived functor of C followed by P. Apply Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso to each integer-indexed homology functor: the hypothesis implies that the ordinary realization of H^i(f) is invertible. Step 3 reflects this to invertibility of H^i(f) for every i. DerivedCategory.isIso_iff then proves IsIso f in the unbounded derived category.

lean.statement:
theorem constantAdicQuotientRealization_reflects_iso_of_map
    (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X)
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (n : ℕ)
    (W : Y.Etale) (_w : W.left)
    (E F : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (AdicCompletion d.ideal A ⧸
      (d.ideal.map (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion d.ideal A))) ^ (n + 1))))
    (f : E ⟶ F)
    (hf : IsIso ((constantAdicQuotientRealization (W.hom ≫ g) d n).map f)) :
    IsIso f
